audit.whatIsWrong: Several fields tell the player to W his dash, or to 'use W to ignore his lack of dashes'. Nasus has no dash anywhere in his kit, so Steadfast Presence's active does nothing to him.
audit.why: The page contradicts itself in one breath — it calls him dash-less and then sells a dash-stop as the trading rule. What W actually gives here is its passive armour and MR, which scale up as Poppy's health drops.
audit.corrected: Dash-denial replaced with the real read: W's passive resists carry the trade, Heroic Charge needs a wall, and Fury of the Sands deals percent health so stacking raw resists is not the counter.

audit.whatIsWrong: Siphoning Strike is an auto-attack reset and Fury of the Sands deals percent-health damage; neither is mentioned.
audit.why: The reset wind-up is the step-back cue, and percent-health damage means armour alone does not answer his ult.
audit.corrected: Both added — the reset tell into the early block, the percent-health warning into mid.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 are yours: Nasus has no dash, no escape, and his only early tool is a slow Q last-hit, so when you hit Lvl 2-3 with Q+E you can E him into the wall for a stun and Q his max HP for a real chunk. Punish every time he walks up to stack his Q on the cannon minion. The thing to respect is Wither — if he W's you mid-trade your attack speed tanks, so open with the E-wall-stun rather than walking in for autos first.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are yours: Nasus has no dash, no escape, and Siphoning Strike is a 255-range auto reset, so the wind-up on his attack is your cue, not the cast. At Lvl 2-3 with Q+E you E him into the wall for a stun and Q his max HP for a real chunk. Punish every walk-up to stack Q on the cannon. Respect Wither — 15s cooldown and it guts your attack speed, so open with the E-wall-stun rather than walking in for autos first.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 stay favourable while your max-HP Q still out-trades his pre-stack damage, so keep zoning him off farm and freezing the wave away from his tower to starve his stacks. At 6 the lane shifts: his R gives armor, size and lifesteal that turn a Withered duel against you, so stop forcing the all-in into his ult and respect the moment he hits it. Trade on your terms with E into a wall, never into open ground where it just shoves him to safety.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stay favourable while your max-HP Q out-trades his pre-stack damage, so keep zoning him off farm and freezing away from his tower to starve stacks. At 6 the lane shifts: Fury of the Sands adds resists, range and percent-health damage on a 120s cooldown, so armour alone is not the answer — stop forcing all-ins into it. Trade on your terms with E into a wall, never into open ground where it just shoves him to safety.

edits.before: Late game belongs to Nasus if he free-farmed — a few hundred Q stacks plus Wither means he out-drains your flat low-base damage and your E-stun isn't enough to kill him. Your job is to make late game never matter: deny stacks early, end the lane on your Lvl 2-3 and first-item windows, and shift to using your W dash-deny and E peel for your carries in fights rather than soloing him. Keep him off objectives and never give him a free side lane to stack uncontested.
edits.after: Late game belongs to Nasus if he free-farmed — hundreds of Q stacks plus Wither out-drain your flat damage and the E-stun alone will not kill him.
